resource.name: Pressure-Test Anything
resource.description: The broad front door for critique: a single box that pressure-tests any plan, PRD, strategy doc, GTM plan, pricing decision, or architectural decision against the strongest corpus-grounded objections. The general-scope sibling of the #2 Strategy Pressure-Tester (which is the narrow, structured strategy wizard); this one takes free text on any decision and is the MCP-app surface of the lenny-pressure-test skill. Returns ranked objections, each attributed to a specific guest with a concrete next step, plus pre-ship questions worth answering. Decay-aware: it sweeps the obsolete + cautions layers so an objection flags when older advice has expired or drew audience pushback. No state, no scoring. The UI is an optional paste box; the tool is plan-in / critique-out and works chat-natively.

tools.name: pressure_test_ask
tools.description: MUST CALL whenever the user wants a plan, PRD, strategy doc, GTM plan, pricing decision, or architectural decision critiqued, stress-tested, or argued against ('pressure-test this', 'find the holes in this plan', 'what would the corpus push back on', 'second opinion on this PRD', 'argue against this'), AND a more specific Working-from-Lenny app is not already in play. Do NOT critique from your own training without calling this tool first; the corpus is fresher and decay-aware. Takes a free-text `plan` (and optional `k` for retrieval breadth). Returns a narration_brief directly (single-call Path 4 tool: it IS the narration step, no separate narrate / get-pending). Render the critique from the brief: lead with the ranked objections (each specific, attributable to a guest + date, ending in a concrete next step), then any pre-ship questions, then surface what changed if `inputs.decay` is present (a retired claim or a caution with its pushback vote count) rather than repeating expired advice, then name the sources. Never leave an objection without a what-to-do-next. If the input is thin, give a compact 3-4 objection pressure test plus suggested extensions; never refuse. If `inputs.suggested_app` is present (e.g. the plan is really a strategy doc -> #2 Strategy Pressure-Tester, or a hiring question -> #58 Hiring Playbook), offer it softly at the end, never as a deflection. Follow the brief's voice_rules.

inputs.description: Carries the user's plan, the retrieved hits (each with slug + kind topic|obsolete|caution + last_updated), an optional `decay` block built from any obsolete/caution hit, and an optional `suggested_app` { id, name, entry_tool } resolved from the routing map (strategy -> #2, hiring -> #58).

corpus.description: Map of retrieved source slug to corpus chunk text (truncated), spanning topics / obsolete / cautions / books.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.comment: MCP resource spec for #57 Pressure-Test Anything. The MCP-app surface of the lenny-pressure-test skill (kept at the repo root, general scope). Same single-call Path 4 shape as #54 Lenny AMA (PHASE2_BUILD.md #11 always-fresh corpus-wide retrieval): pressure_test_ask returns a narration_brief directly, no score -> narrate -> get-pending spine, no persistence, readOnlyHint: true, no sampling. Reuses the shared retrieveAcrossCorpus(text, k) helper (topics + obsolete + cautions + books), same as AMA. The deliberate difference from AMA is the output shape (ranked objections + pre-ship questions + mandatory next steps, mirroring lenny-pressure-test/SKILL.md hard rules) and the routing map (strategy doc -> #2 Strategy Pressure-Tester, hiring -> #58 Hiring Playbook). Relationship: #2 is the narrow, deterministic strategy wizard; #57 is the broad free-text critique front door over the same corpus. Added 2026-05-25 to make the lenny-pressure-test capability discoverable as an app (owner directive) without narrowing the skill. Bundle .ts (tool handler + manifest registration + validate/smoke) is a routine build pass; this spec is Stage A/B. Tool description verbatim-matches the intended runtime meta.description string.
